videos.script: Ponto Final has a loyalty card, and four and a half thousand people carry it. Some of them are about to stop coming. {{shop}} Marketing wants to send those people a voucher before they go. So somebody has to say, for every member, how likely that is. {{question}} You could write a rule. No visit in four months means gone. It is one line, and it is wrong both ways. {{rule}} Or you could let a program read last year's members, and what became of each one, and learn the rule itself. That program's output is a model. {{model}} The modeller picks the algorithm. Almost everything else is the platform's job. Which rows it learns from. How each number is computed. Where the model lives, and how anyone finds out it has stopped being right. {{platform}} That is this course. A data engineer's view of a model. {{course}} This lesson builds your lab, on your own computer, and draws the shop into it. {{lab}} Then it trains three things. A model that learns from answers. One that finds groups with no answers at all. And one that learns by trying. {{three}} By the end you will know which kind a question needs. And when it needs none. {{end}}
